name: His Name Is Alive
label: 4AD
lede: A Michigan teenager taped songs in his parents' basement, mailed them to 4AD until Ivo Watts-Russell said yes, and cried when he heard what Ivo did with them. Decades later Warren Defever is still the only constant in His Name Is Alive.

eras.title: A basement in Livonia
eras.text: Livonia, Michigan, as Defever describes it, is a grid of numbered roads with nothing to do. He put on headphones and started recording alone in his parents' basement, and kept mailing the results to a label in London that kept saying no.

years.src: Arcane Delights · It's Psychedelic Baby · Wikipedia: His Name Is Alive
years.h: A high schooler starts taping songs under the house
years.p: Warren Defever records alone on a 4-track cassette deck, with friend Angie Carozzo singing. Many songs are first takes, often the first time he'd played them.
years.xp:
The kit was minimal: guitar, a sampler, vocals and a Radio Shack PZM microphone, with no drums and no mixer, according to the Arcane Delights interview. Recording got interrupted by whatever the household was doing upstairs.

Defever says he turned inward rather than taking up petty crime like the other bored kids: "I was a curious child exploring all the options."

years.src: Wikipedia: His Name Is Alive · Arcane Delights · It's Psychedelic Baby
years.h: Ivo Watts-Russell rejects the tapes, then signs the band
years.p: Defever keeps sending 4AD improved versions of the same songs, one tape titled I Had Sex With God. Ivo prefers the ones sung by Karin Oliver, whom Defever met at college, and signs them in 1989.
years.xp: Ivo's bet was that he and [[John Fryer|17375716-41de-49a9-8b9c-64c71bb14742]], his partner in [[This Mortal Coil|60ef8ddb-7676-4056-a357-9a8c228d03a6]], could remix the basement recordings into a proper 4AD album. Defever says he had no idea his songs lacked choruses or a normal length.

eras.title: Ivo takes it apart
eras.text: Ivo and Fryer rebuilt the home tapes at Blackwing Studios in London, and Livonia became one of 4AD's best sellers that year. By the third album Defever was mixing his own records and touring with a band.

years.big: "He took it apart, and he didn't put it back together."
q: I cried and said, 'Wow, it's a million times better!'
years.src: Wikipedia: Livonia · Arcane Delights · Wikipedia: His Name Is Alive
years.p: Defever on Ivo's production. Mixed by Ivo and Fryer at Blackwing, it's one of the label's biggest sellers of 1990; Defever's own summary is "fucked up minimalism, arranged classically."
years.xp:
The basement tapes were bumped up to an 8-track reel-to-reel at a friend's studio, which added room for bass, bass clarinet and percussion. When he heard Ivo and Fryer's mix, Defever says, "I cried and said, 'Wow, it's a million times better!'"

Carozzo is credited but barely heard, and left after the release. Rykodisc put Livonia out in the US in 1992.

yt: Live at the Majestic Theatre, Detroit, 1990
years.h: The first shows at the Majestic Theater are just guitar and voice
years.p: No band yet: Defever on guitar, Oliver singing.

years.src: Wikipedia: Home Is in Your Head
years.h: Home Is in Your Head: 23 tracks in 48 minutes
years.p: More basement 4-track, again remixed by Ivo and Fryer. The hidden track, The Other Body, stops dead where the tape ran out.
years.xp: Five years later Cameron Crowe used Sitting Still Moving Still Staring Outlooking in a key scene of Jerry Maguire (1996).

years.src: Wikipedia: His Name Is Alive · Arcane Delights
yt: Are We Still Married?, Brothers Quay
years.h: The Brothers Quay say no to music videos, then make two
years.p: 4AD lets the Quay twins pick their songs: they choose Are We Still Married? and later Can't Go Wrong Without You. The films end up in MoMA exhibitions.
years.xp: "They said they would never do a music video but...called the next day saying they couldn't believe the music," Defever told Arcane Delights.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mouth by Mouth · It's Psychedelic Baby · Wikipedia: His Name Is Alive
yt: Can't Go Wrong Without You, official video
years.h: Mouth by Mouth is the first one Defever mixes himself
years.p: Noisier pop, four lead singers and a [[Big Star|21d177ba-3d51-461e-9b3f-ad9a80b419dc]] cover, Blue Moon. Robert Christgau gives it an A minus; the US CD drops the samples and changes mixes to reach grunge audiences.
years.xp: By now Defever had drum machines, samplers and five singers on call. He sampled Jack Nicholson and Prince dialogue freely: "There's a line somewhere between copying, stealing, and a loving tribute."

years.src: Wikipedia: His Name Is Alive · Arcane Delights
years.h: Twenty-eight shows across North America with drummer Trey Many
years.p: The first full tour: Defever on guitar, Oliver singing, [[Trey Many|94f62f1b-5855-4739-806e-08b40ea817bc]] on drums. The band rearranges the records so much the songs come out new.

eras.title: Dub, surf and Pet Sounds
eras.text: Defever spent three years on the fourth album, collaging dub, surf, country and the Beach Boys. Then 4AD changed hands, the contract got more traditional, and so did the record that followed.

years.h: Defever's mother dies, and the next album waits
years.p: Wikipedia's account of Stars on E.S.P. lists her death, the 1993 tour and unfinished side projects as the reasons it took from December 1992 to finish.

years.src: Wikipedia: Stars on E.S.P. · Wikipedia: His Name Is Alive
years.h: Defever calls Universal Frequencies a sequel to Good Vibrations
years.p: Stars on E.S.P. is the breakthrough: songs co-written with [[Mark Kozelek|99f4b23d-3711-4efe-ad71-9572158e234c]], [[Ian Masters|07d80ea6-ecd1-42c3-9ca1-3a90e683ea81]] of [[Pale Saints|1584532a-62ed-4cbe-ad95-6def0af7df35]], Matthew Smith of Outrageous Cherry and Erika Hoffmann. Entertainment Weekly gives it an A.
years.xp: Lovetta Pippen, an experienced soul and gospel singer, first turns up here in a gospel choir. Within five years she'd be the band's lead voice.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ft. Lake · Wikipedia: His Name Is Alive
years.h: A producer who worked with Aretha Franklin makes Ft. Lake
years.p: Steve King, who'd worked with Franklin and George Clinton, is the band's first outside producer. With 4AD's change of ownership came a traditional contract, and a deliberately accessible record.
years.xp: Defever stepped back to songwriting and guitar. Wikipedia says that when Ft. Lake fell short of the label's new commercial expectations, most of the band left for day jobs or other projects.

eras.title: Soul records, and out
eras.text: Down to Defever and Lovetta Pippen, His Name Is Alive made two soul and R&B records that lost some of the dream-pop crowd. Then 4AD let them go.

years.h: Lovetta Pippen takes over the microphone
years.p: The duo's first album trades the ethereal sound for soul and R&B.

years.h: After Last Night, 4AD drops His Name Is Alive
years.p: Twelve years and about 100,000 albums sold for the label, by Wikipedia's count.

eras.title: His own label, his own studio
eras.text: Defever kept the name going on his Time Stereo and Silver Mountain labels and in Detroit's music scene, then went back to the 4AD tapes himself at Third Man Mastering.

years.cap: His Name Is Alive live, February 2006
years.h: Detrola brings in a new voice, Andy FM
years.p: The first full-length on Defever's Silver Mountain Media, distributed by Sony BMG, introduces Andy FM, keyboardist for Detroit's Tranzistors. Pippen and Hoffmann guest.

years.cap: His Name Is Alive live in Detroit, March 2007
years.h: Sweet Earth Flower pays tribute to Marion Brown
years.p: A His Name Is Alive album of the free-jazz saxophonist's music, on High Two.

years.h: A 20th anniversary with a missing year
years.p: Defever marks 20 years with shows and a community bike ride in Detroit, though the first record came out in 1990. One year, he says, has been blacked out, for reasons he won't discuss.

years.src: Bandcamp: How Ghosts Affect Relationships · It's Psychedelic Baby
years.h: How Ghosts Affect Relationships boxes up the first four years
years.p: Six LPs, 77 tracks, 1,000 numbered copies, remastered by Defever at Third Man Mastering from the analogue tapes, with a book by 4AD biographer Martin Aston.
